title: Monotonicity of time bounds
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $T_1,T_2\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ has total nonhalting probability at most $T_1(|x|)$ on every input $x$ and every halted run outputs the one-symbol indicator of whether $x\in L$, and if $T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then $N$ has total nonhalting probability at most $T_2(|x|)$ on every input and retains the same output condition on every halted run.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$N$ satisfies the stated nonhalting-probability bound with $T_1$
Every halted run outputs the one-symbol indicator of membership in $L$
